All sorted, cleanly on both sides:

**For you, once per machine:**
```
git config --global core.autocrlf false
```
That's the setting that was generating every one of those warnings — it told git to rewrite LF files to CRLF in your working tree, and git was dutifully warning about each impending rewrite. `false` is the right modern choice on Windows; everything in your toolchain handles LF natively.

**For the repo, permanently:** `.gitattributes` now pins `* text=auto eol=lf` (with binary exceptions), which makes line endings the *repo's* decision — no future contributor's or machine's config can flip them. This matters more here than in a typical project: blob SHAs key the embedding cache and ledger scope items, so a CRLF-flipped file would silently count as brand-new content and re-embed. The renormalize pass found exactly one offender — `CLAUDE.md`, from a hand edit — fixed with content untouched. And the proof was immediate: the commit landing this fix was the first in the project's history with zero CRLF warnings.

CLAUDE.md is also updated to match the new reality: warnings were "normal noise" before; from now on, if one appears it means something is writing CRLF and the *writer* should be fixed, not the warning silenced.

Ready to pick up desktop build-order step 2 (the branch/diff API groundwork) whenever you are.

Fair point taken, both parts. (And on the config: skipping the global setting is fine — the repo's `.gitattributes` overrides it here, so the warnings stay gone in this repo regardless.)

You're right about the pattern, and I'll own it: the plan kept Electron last behind "groundwork," and that was my sequencing, twice deferred. You want an actual application — an icon you launch, a window you own, not a command that borrows a browser tab. Flipping the order now: **the Electron shell is the current task**, and the API/branch work becomes things that land *inside* an app you already have. Launching the build:

attributes.command: cd C:/src/git-for-ai && grep -n "export.*function runReview\|export interface ReviewOptions" packages/cli/src/commands/review.ts | head -4 && grep -n "port\|listen\|close" packages/cli/src/commands/review.ts | head -10

The Electron app is being built right now, as the priority. To be concrete about what "the app exists" means when this lands, because it's more than the web view with a frame:

- **You launch it like software**: `pnpm --filter @git-for-ai/desktop start` opens a real window — no terminal command per repo, no browser, no borrowed tab. (Installer packaging via electron-builder is configured but deliberately not built today; running from source is the deliverable, the installer is a follow-up once you've used it.)
- **It owns your repos, plural**: first launch shows a repo picker (native folder dialog + a remembered recent-repos list). Pick a repo that isn't opted in yet and you get a plain-language screen with an **Initialize** button — the app can onboard a repo itself, no CLI required.
- **The server becomes an implementation detail**: the app starts it internally on a random localhost port, points its own window at it, and shuts it down cleanly when you close the window — nothing left running (your rule).
- **Proper desktop hygiene**: remembered window size/position, single-instance lock, standard menu, and Electron's security posture done right (context isolation on, no node access leaking into the page).

And to be fair to the architecture while owning the sequencing mistake: the SPA-inside-Electron shape was always the design — the part I got wrong was treating the shell as the *last* step instead of the thing that makes everything else feel real to you. With the shell in hand, the remaining DESKTOP.md items — branch sidebar, diff-with-intent view, the actions panel — each land as visible upgrades to an app already on your machine, rather than promises about one.

The agent's bar for "done" includes actually launching the app against this repo and proving clean startup and shutdown from its logs. When it reports, I'll verify, commit, and hand you the start command.
The Electron shell is built with launch evidence. Verifying independently — build, tests, and running the real smoke myself:

attributes.command: cd C:/src/git-for-ai && pnpm turbo build 2>&1 | grep "Tasks:" && cd packages/desktop && pnpm vitest run 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests " && pnpm smoke 2>&1 | grep -E "\[desktop\]|EXIT" | head -8

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && powershell -c "if (Get-Process electron -EA SilentlyContinue) {'ORPHANS PRESENT'} else {'no orphan processes'}" && git add packages/desktop pnpm-workspace.yaml pnpm-lock.yaml README.md architecture/DESKTOP.md && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
The desktop app exists: Electron shell around the review server + SPA

Owner priority override of DESKTOP.md's build order - the shell ships
first so the app is real now; the branch/diff/actions work lands
inside it next. packages/desktop:

- main.ts: single-instance Electron main starting the review server
  in-process (127.0.0.1, random port) and pointing its window at it;
  remembered window bounds + last repo; standard menu; graceful
  awaited server shutdown on close/quit - verified zero orphan
  processes after real launches.
- Repo picker: native folder dialog + recent list (userData JSON),
  plus the uninitialized-repo opt-in screen wired to the CLI's pure
  runInit - the one write action; the served surface stays read-only.
- Security posture: contextIsolation on, nodeIntegration off, sandbox
  on; the 3-verb preload bridge (pickFolder/openRepo/init) is gated to
  the local picker page only - the served SPA gets no privileges.
  window.open denied; navigation confined.
- --smoke self-verification seam: launch -> open repo -> /api/meta ->
  clean quit, exit 0. Run live against this repo by the agent and
  re-run independently before commit (server started, SPA titled,
  meta returned head, clean close).
- electron-builder.yml checked in (win/nsis, placeholder appId per the
  naming-TBD decision); installer deliberately not built yet.

Zero changes to packages/cli - startReviewServer was already
programmatic. 18 new tests (state store, repo validation - real
fixture repos, real runInit). Full build 5/5, tests 10/10 tasks.

Launch: pnpm --filter @git-for-ai/desktop start

Implemented by a background Fable 5 agent; independently re-verified
(build, tests, live smoke, orphan check) and committed by the
orchestrating session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
